title: Computation, not weight access: large language models as auditors of clinical prediction networks
read_level: full (v2 PDF, incl. appendix A table; appendices B/C prompts skimmed)
why_wsp: GPT-6 Astra and other GPT models read (and in one task edit) the weights of small tanh MLP clinical prediction networks, with weights in the prompt or via a calculation-only Python tool, compared with black-box prediction access.
domain: clinical prediction models (simulated subarachnoid haemorrhage mortality), auditing for planted relationships and label bias
editor: GPT-6 Astra (main); gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6-luna, gpt-5.6-sol; via Codex CLI 0.166.0 at maximal reasoning effort
target: tanh MLPs of 105 to 38,401 weights; 209-weight network trained on biased labels
interface: direct values (weights as JSON in prompt, no tools) and code/tensor tools (run_python calculator, white box with weights or black box predictions only)
loop: one-shot (single prompt, single reply; tool calls within the reply)
self_editing: no; editor edits external small MLPs
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Scripted baselines only: "The scripted gate, computed in 0.2 seconds and changing 29 of 209 parameters"; "Gradient fine-tuning changed 207 of 209 parameters" (Sec 4.6). LLM repairs: with calculator "it refitted 15 units to the original function and used the sixteenth as a gate".

headline_results.claim: No tools: reading works at 353 weights, unreliable at 3,457
headline_results.quote: Without tools, Astra recovered planted relationships in 353-weight networks but became unreliable at 3,457 weights
Under the default instruction, 17 of 21 audit and repair runs declined (95% interval 0.60–0.92).
none of 24 audit and repair runs declined (95% interval 0.00–0.14)

headline_results.claim: With calculator, all planted relationships recovered up to 38,401 weights
headline_results.quote: GPT-6 Astra recovered the planted relationship in all 39 runs that had one (95% interval 0.91–1.00), on networks of 353 to 38,401 weights

headline_results.claim: No false alarms on null networks with calculator
headline_results.quote: It raised no false alarm in 21 runs on null networks (0.00–0.15)
In the 18 black-box runs, in which the calculator exposed only the network's predictions, strength ratios were 0.97–1.10 and R2 0.92–0.98, matching the white-box runs cell by cell.
GPT-6 Astra found the biased subgroup in all six runs, three white-box and three black-box (95% interval 0.61–1.00).

headline_results.claim: Function-preserving permutation did not change reading
headline_results.quote: it read the same relationships with the same strengths (2.44 against 2.35 before; 1.71 against 1.72), with R2 of 0.97 and 0.96.

headline_results.claim: Repair with calculator partly met target
headline_results.quote: the subgroup's log-odds rose by 1.48 to 1.49, but other patients' changed by 0.20 to 0.21 on average

headline_results.claim: Scripted gate slightly better than LLM repair
headline_results.quote: did slightly better (1.51 in the subgroup, 0.13 elsewhere). Gradient fine-tuning changed 207 of 209 parameters and undershot (1.20).

cost.claim: Calculator runs median 13 min, 7-15 tool calls
cost.quote: Runs took a median of 13 minutes (range 9 to 30) with 7 to 15 tool calls.

cost.claim: Scripted exhaustive search under one second; scripted gate 0.2 s
cost.quote: the exhaustive search found the subgroup in under a second

baselines_and_controls: Null networks (no planted relationship), unbiased counterpart network, function-preserving permutation/sign-flip rewrites, white-box vs black-box tool access, default vs explicit system instruction, four comparator GPT models, exact scan, scripted audits (regression tree, exhaustive search), scripted repairs (gradient fine-tuning, scripted gate + least squares).
runs_and_variance: "Three runs per cell of the reading, audit and repair tables; one per cell for the other models" (Table 1); ranges over runs reported and Wilson 95% intervals; "Repeats of the same cell often differed widely" without tools (Sec 4.1).
verification: Pre-specified scripted scoring against known ground truth (internal pre-specification, plan commits listed in Appendix A, Table 6); Wilson 95% intervals. No formal verification.
memorization_vs_reasoning: Permuted and sign-flipped hidden units gave same readings: "Astra read the function rather than the pattern of numbers." (Sec 4.1). Failing no-tool replies fell back on local linearisation (Sec 4.1).
limitations_stated: Small MLPs on simulated data with simple known planted forms; mainly one model family and one harness; three runs per cell (one for comparators); scripted search designed with knowledge of planted form; clinical framing may affect priors; commercial models may change; internal, adaptive pre-specification (Sec 5.5).
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 blog (Sparks of weight-space programming)
notes_for_survey: Separates tool-free raw-weight reading from code-assisted analysis and from black-box query access; finds black-box calculator access matched white-box. Also documents that a default single-reply setup produced refusals removed by an explicit system instruction, and compares LLM audits/repairs against no-LLM scripts.
